items.quote: This program changed my life. I found my confidence here.
Skateboarding saved my life. Now we're saving others.
I never thought I'd be a mentor. ODA showed me the way.

partners.name: The Frederick Douglass Community Association
partners.desc: "The Doug" has donated in-kind facilities, staff support, and countless other resources to ODA, providing a space to work, learn, and a valuable network of connections for students and staffers.

partners.name: City of Toledo Youth Services
partners.desc: The City of Toledo's Youth Programming Grant was pivotal in the "I Can" Program with a $15,000 donation in 2023, funding a skatepark build, PPE for students, and staff salaries.

partners.name: The DUBS Foundation
partners.desc: Austin and Nick Weber build skate ramps and obstacles for class use and the D.I.Y. park in Toledo, and help create and support events for the "I Can" Program.

partners.name: Advocate Skateworks
partners.desc: Travis at ASW helped ODA secure Vans skate shoes and an invaluable number of skateboard decks for students through his relationships with notable skate companies.

partners.name: Pizza Cat Toledo
partners.desc: Pizza Cat donated THIRTY pizzas for the 2024 4 Cs Games fundraiser. Their mission aligns with ODA — rebuilding the local community through the youth within it.

partners.name: Nuclear Skate Cult
partners.desc: Toledo's premier skate team has supported ODA since day one by sponsoring events, recruiting coaches, and promoting the mission to empower Toledo's youth through skateboarding.

partners.name: Steez LLC
partners.desc: Steez is a local skate company known for butter-smooth skate wax and street apparel, donating prizes for ODA events and contests.

partners.name: Lavish Hardware
partners.desc: Lavish is a local skate company known for rock-solid hardware and unique apparel. They support ODA with prizes for competitions and events to keep the "I Can" Program running.

partners.name: Modern Skate Shop
partners.desc: Detroit, Michigan-based skate shop and indoor park. Modern contributes prizes for ODA events and fundraisers, helping strengthen the Toledo skateboarding community.

partners.name: Just Skateboarding
partners.desc: Toledo's local skate shop. Owner Scott Tutek provides skateboarding supplies, equipment, and apparel plus deep roots in the local skate scene.

partners.name: Ryno's Skate Shop
partners.desc: Fremont, Ohio-based skate shop donating prizes for contests and events while strengthening ODA's connections to the Fremont skateboarding community.

partners.name: Lil Jawns Skateboard Rails
partners.desc: Texas-based, skater-owned company supporting skateboarding as a culture and community. Donated prizes for ODA fundraising events and contests.

partners.name: Vans
partners.desc: Vans is a well-known brand in the skate community. ODA received a donation of skate shoes, tee shirts, and over 100 skateboard decks from Vans.

partners.name: Printed on a Lark
partners.desc: Toledo-based screen printing company. Emilia taught ODA screen printing, giving the program the ability to create apparel, raise funds, and teach students a marketable skill.

partners.name: Smollie Skateboard Co.
partners.desc: Smollie donated training straps used in every "I Can" classroom session, giving students a safe and realistic skateboarding experience as they develop their skills.

partners.name: Keen Ramps
partners.desc: Long Beach, CA-based skate company. Keen Ramps donated a ledge and ramps used in every "I Can" class, providing safe, realistic skatepark obstacles for students.

partners.name: Indo Board Balance Boards
partners.desc: Indo Board donated balance boards to the "I Can" Program — a vital training tool strengthening students' balance skills and board control.
